newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht under pressure from Moody's.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht under pressure from Moody's.

text.p: Dollar stayed firm against most regional currencies in Friday morning trade.
Moody's potential downgrading of Thailand's A2 long-term foreign currency debt ceiling triggered some selling of baht against the greenback, dealers said.
"Some offshore players begun to sell off the baht again after the Moody's announcement. It added another negative note to the baht," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
At 0400 GMT, the baht was at 26.055/065 to the dollar against 25.990/26.001 late on Thursday.
Moody said the review was prompted by concerns over Thailand's financial sector, where there is a huge concentration of short-term foreign currency debt.
Continued weakness of the Thai stock market also triggered dollar buying, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate unchanged at 25.98 per a dollar, the lowest level since May 4, 1990.
Some analysts said the baht could test 26.50 to the dollar if the dollar continued to strengthen towards 140 yen.
The increase in Singapore's foreign reserves to S$107.75 billion in December from S$106.3 billion in November made little impact on the Singapore currency.

"(It) was seen consistent with market perception that the Monetary Authority of Singapore might have been buying the dollar against the Singapore dollar to slow the appreciation of the local currency," an analyst at MMS said.
The Singapore dollar was steady at 1.4178/88 to the dollar at 0400 GMT.
The Indonesian rupiah declined slightly against the dollar in slow early trading as excess rupiah supply continued to haunt the market, dealers said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,381.0/2.0 at 0400 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,379.20/79.70.
One Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta said swap rates softened across the board following relatively ample liquidity.

Overnight swaps fell to 1.25 from 2.2 points. Spot/next were last given at 0.45 points. The dealer said swaps less than one-month were likely to ease further on liquidity issue, while the downside for longer-term swaps was limited.
"The upcoming general election on May 29 would also limit the six-month swap to fall below the 78-point support level," the Japanese bank dealer said.
Dealers said central bank dollar buying on Wednesday, estimated at around $600 million, seemed to have helped keep the market liquid, aided by moderate tax payments due Friday.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,377/2,569. The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week and three points the previous week.
The ringgit traded in a narrow range due to a lack of interest from foreign players, dealers said.
But, additional requirement for Malaysia's surging stock market and foreign funds looking for higher yields are expected to boost the ringgit next week, they said.
However, there was strong resistance at 2.48 a dollar level, which if overcome could see ringgit heading higher. At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4850/60 to a dollar.
-- Madhav Reddy in KL (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
